# `dump --stage checked` prints a method call and a call site's type
# arguments back so the dump checks again.
#
# A method whose receiver its parameters do not list -- a `sngl:` method's,
# one on a generic type -- was printed in the static form,
# `list.map(xs, fn=…)` and `Test.assert(t, b=…)`, which hands the receiver to
# the first parameter: "cannot pass list[int] as func(int) string". It prints
# as it was written now (ir.Call.ReceiverArg). Type arguments a call wrote
# print with it, and a generic struct's literal says its arguments, so a
# return-only parameter and a context's stated type survive the round trip.

sngl dump --stage checked app.sngl
cp stdout first.sngl
sngl check first.sngl
sngl dump --stage checked first.sngl
cp stdout second.sngl
cmp first.sngl second.sngl

grep '\[1, 2\]\.map\[string\]\(' first.sngl
grep 't\.assert\(b=' first.sngl
grep 'empty\[string\]\(\)' first.sngl
grep 'Box\[int\]\{value=3\}' first.sngl
grep 'context\[option\[User\]\] #who\(null\)' first.sngl

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

struct User {
    name string
}

struct Box[T any] {
    value T
}

func empty[T any]() list[T] {
    var xs list[T] = []
    return xs
}

context[option[User]] #who(null)

component main node {
    var box = Box[int]{value=3}
    text(value="{box.value}")
}

func testRoundTrip(t Test, c main) {
    var names = [1, 2].map[string](func(n) => "{n}")
    var xs = empty[string]()
    t.assert(names.length == 2 && xs.length == 0)
}

window {
    main
}
